protocol.purpose: find which real objects the existing controllable-Sharpe generator already resembles, so the NEXT small calibration has a target. This stage fits nothing.

nasdaq100.label: Nasdaq-100
nasdaq100.chosen_because: same country and calendar, different composition -- separates composition from window

nikkei225.label: Nikkei 225
nikkei225.chosen_because: a different exchange calendar and a different crisis timing

ff_momentum.label: Momentum factor (daily)
ff_momentum.chosen_because: a long-short STRATEGY return rather than a price index; chosen for the type it adds, not for how it fits

models.stoch_vol: pure SV at the recorded A = 1, rho = 0.98

protocol.no_search: every shape parameter is the value already in config.py; the only quantity estimated per object is its overall scale

transforms.price_index: simple daily return P_t/P_(t-1) - 1 between consecutive trading days, decimals
transforms.factor_return: the published daily factor return, percent converted to decimal once on load; never differenced and never compounded into a price first
transforms.forbidden: no forward fill, no monthly series interpolated to daily, no winsorising

periods.contrast_role: a frozen-parameter development contrast. It is development data that has already been examined, not a new independent test.
periods.excluded: 2024-2025 takes no part in any statistic, figure or choice this round

scale_handling.per_object: sigma_annual = sd(returns in the describe window) * sqrt(252), estimated separately for each object
scale_handling.frozen: the SAME scale is used for the contrast period. The later period's realised volatility never rescales a main result.
scale_handling.level_versus_shape: the RV_21 quantiles are reported TWICE and the two must not be confused. As LEVELS they compare the market and the simulation at the same frozen sigma_annual. As SHAPE they are divided by the series' OWN annualised sd -- and for a simulation that ratio is formed INSIDE each path before any quantile is taken across paths, because dividing every path by one common number is a different quantity.
scale_handling.cross_market_shape: scale-free statistics (tails, ACF, W1 on standardised returns, concentration, lead-lag) are compared directly; the volatility range is compared through the per-path shape ratio above.
scale_handling.no_unified_leaderboard: stage 4's per-branch standardised total loss is NOT reused here and no object is ranked by a single total score.

distribution_and_tails: W1 on standardised daily returns with a simulation-to-simulation reference
tail frequency AND raw count at 2 sd, each side
tail frequency AND raw count at 3 sd, each side
tail frequency AND raw count at 5 sd, each side
diagnostics.nothing_else: no statistic was added or removed after seeing a result

simulation.tag: blake2b(object, model, period) -- stable across processes
simulation.initialisation: stationary; no path is rescaled after the draw

figures: one figure on the volatility-persistence gap, which stages 2-4 identified as the core mismatch
protocol.stopping_condition: stop once every object has been contrasted against the three fixed models over both periods and the gap table exists. No re-run with different settings, whatever the result.
protocol.range_semantics: a simulated range is the spread of a statistic under a FIXED model; it is not a market-parameter confidence interval, being inside it does not make a model correct, and being outside it does not identify a missing mechanism.
not_in_this_stage: declaring a best-fitting market on a total score

code_identity.pythonhashseed_env: not set (and no longer relied on)

objects.defects: 1 price(s) printed on a day the calendar says the exchange was closed (2019-04-19) -- dropped at the analysis layer, the next return re-formed from the adjacent valid closes

sp500.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED); index by S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC
sp500.frequency: daily, business days (Mon-Fri), blank on US market holidays
sp500.units: index level, points (S&P 500 PRICE index; dividends excluded)
sp500.redistribution: S&P Dow Jones Indices data; FRED states it may not be redistributed. Raw and per-day derived files stay local.

nasdaq100.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED); index by Nasdaq, Inc.
nasdaq100.frequency: daily, business days, blank on US market holidays
nasdaq100.units: index level, points (PRICE index; dividends excluded)
nasdaq100.redistribution: Nasdaq index data via FRED; kept local with the rest.

nikkei225.role: cross-market, price index, different exchange calendar
nikkei225.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED); index by Nikkei Inc.
nikkei225.frequency: daily, business days, blank on Japanese market holidays
nikkei225.units: index level, points (PRICE index; dividends excluded)
nikkei225.calendar_note: an encoded JPX rule set now provides the expected trading days INDEPENDENTLY of the observed dates: New Year and year end, the fixed and nth-weekday national holidays, the listed equinoxes, the 2019 abdication and enthronement days (2019-04-30, 05-01, 05-02, 10-22) and the 2020-2021 Olympic moves. It is a rule set written here, not an authoritative exchange calendar, so it is cross-checked against the source file's blanks and the disagreements are reported. Over 2017-2023 the two agree on all 114 weekday closures, including the 2019 Golden Week.
nikkei225.redistribution: Nikkei index data via FRED; kept local with the rest.

ff_momentum.role: cross-market, a long-short FACTOR RETURN rather than a price index
ff_momentum.provider: Kenneth R. French data library (Tuck School of Business)
ff_momentum.units: daily factor RETURN in PERCENT; 0.55 means 0.55%, i.e. 0.0055. Converted to a decimal once on load and never again.
ff_momentum.definition: MOM = average return of the two high-prior-return value-weight portfolios minus the average of the two low-prior-return portfolios, prior return measured from day -250 to -21. A zero-investment long-short portfolio return, NOT a price index and NOT net of any cost.
ff_momentum.redistribution: free for research use under the library's terms; kept local with the rest and not redistributed here.

sp500.return_definition: P_t / P_(t-1) - 1, consecutive trading days on the nyse calendar

defects: 1 price(s) printed on a day the calendar says the exchange was closed (2019-04-19) -- dropped at the analysis layer, the next return re-formed from the adjacent valid closes
nasdaq100.return_definition: P_t / P_(t-1) - 1, consecutive trading days on the nyse calendar

nikkei225.return_definition: P_t / P_(t-1) - 1, consecutive trading days on the jpx calendar

ff_momentum.return_definition: the published daily factor return, converted from percent to decimal once; NOT differenced, NOT compounded into a price
ff_momentum.gap_note: a factor return is already a one-day quantity, so the gap column is 1 by construction; the DATE SET is what is checked
